messages.author: fdaa54d30ab7b913
messages.subject: Question about model parameterization for occupancy analysis in unmarked
parts:
Dear list members,

I am doing an occupancy analysis for multiple species (4 species) using species as a factor in my models.

I am fitting a model with p different for the 4 species and with psi for each species interacting with a continuos covariate ("dpn").

I have 2 models that I have trouble interpreting the output, mod12e500 and mod13e500.

The first model has the parameterization "~ dpn:esp" for occupancy and the second is the same model but without the intercept for psi: "~ -1 + dpn:esp".  My questions are after the models.

> mod12e500 <- occu(~esp ~ dpn:esp, occe500)
> summary(mod12e500)

Call:
occu(formula = ~esp ~ dpn:esp, data = occe500)

Occupancy (logit-scale):
             Estimate    SE      z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)     2.462 0.931  2.645 0.00817
dpn:espcuni    -0.670 0.250 -2.677 0.00742
dpn:espdasy    -0.150 0.177 -0.849 0.39585
dpn:espdidel   -0.404 0.184 -2.190 0.02851
dpn:esptama    -0.202 0.324 -0.625 0.53200

Detection (logit-scale):
            Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)   -1.825 0.347 -5.26 1.47e-07
espdasy        1.358 0.378  3.60 3.23e-04
espdidel       0.611 0.410  1.49 1.36e-01
esptama       -1.266 0.570 -2.22 2.63e-02

AIC: 591.054 
Number of sites: 56
optim convergence code: 0
optim iterations: 39 
Bootstrap iterations: 0 


> mod13e500 <- occu(~esp ~ -1 + dpn:esp, occe500)
> summary(mod13e500)

Call:
occu(formula = ~esp ~ -1 + dpn:esp, data = occe500)

Occupancy (logit-scale):
             Estimate    SE      z P(>|z|)
dpn:espcuni   -0.2049 0.134 -1.532  0.1254
dpn:espdasy    0.2425 0.137  1.776  0.0757
dpn:espdidel  -0.0168 0.098 -0.172  0.8637
dpn:esptama    3.4791 6.634  0.524  0.6000

Detection (logit-scale):
            Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)   -1.790 0.335 -5.35 8.94e-08
espdasy        1.323 0.366  3.61 3.03e-04
espdidel       0.594 0.397  1.50 1.35e-01
esptama       -1.487 0.495 -3.00 2.66e-03

AIC: 597.1103 
Number of sites: 56
optim convergence code: 0
optim iterations: 65 
Bootstrap iterations: 0 


My interpretation of p is very straightforward, each species has a different p and the intercep is the p for the reference level (species espcuni).

But what about the parameterization for psi? should I have a model with or without the intercept if I want to show different psi for each species and using "dpn" as a covariate influencing psi?

Thank you very much in advance,

Best,

Manuel

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Question about model parameterization for occupancy analysis in unmarked
parts:
Hi Manuel,

I think you do want to estimate the intercept. Otherwise you are assuming that the intercept on the logit-scale is 0, which means p=0.5 when your covariate=0. This is just like a ANCOVA model (with a logit-link). You can use your fitted model to obtain predicted occupancy for each species at specific values of your covariate.

Hope this helps.

Richard

messages.author: 9548b9e0c8258268
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Question about model parameterization for occupancy analysis in unmarked
parts:
Manuel,

An ANCOVA includes an effect for each species level and a single coefficient for dpn, something like this:

occu(~esp ~ -1 +  esp + dpn, occe500)

You didn't really say, but I have a feeling that you actually want both an intercept and dpn covariate slope for each species:

occu(~esp ~ -1 + esp * dpn, occe500)

Note that I omitted the intercept for both models just to parameterize in terms of a separate intercept per species.

Hope that helps,
Ian
